legacy_cells.B: Bayesian Deep Learning for Measurement Error Correction in Health Survey Data
legacy_cells.I: 066_2026_Bayesian Deep Learning for Measurement Error Correction in Health Survey Data.pdf
legacy_cells.S: Predict a binary health outcome from covariates subject to measurement error; child stunting is the example outcome.
legacy_cells.AI: Simulated structured health-survey covariates; binary health outcome
legacy_cells.AJ: Deep neural network with multiple layers (layer count unspecified)
legacy_cells.AN: Latent true covariates with an explicit additive measurement-error observation model
legacy_cells.DX: Table 1: accuracy 0.87; AUC 0.91; log-loss 0.39; calibration error 0.034 (proposed BDL). Table 2 AUC: low noise 0.91, medium 0.88, high 0.84 (proposed BDL).
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with LR, Bayesian logistic regression with measurement error (BLR-ME), and standard deep learning (DL); Table 1 reports BDL accuracy 0.87, AUC 0.91, log-loss 0.39, calibration error 0.034.
legacy_cells.FM: Proposes a Bayesian deep-learning framework combining latent true covariates, measurement-error modeling, nonlinear prediction, and uncertainty quantification.
legacy_cells.FN: In the reported simulation, BDL achieved accuracy 0.87, AUC 0.91, log-loss 0.39, calibration error 0.034; reported 95% interval coverage was 94.2%.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors note MCMC inference is computationally expensive and that priors and model architecture require careful specification.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors propose more efficient inference algorithms, automated model selection, and expansion to geographical and longitudinal data and more health outcomes.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify a gap: existing deep-learning approaches often do not model input measurement error together with uncertainty quantification.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is limited to simulated static binary-outcome prediction. The paper does not demonstrate longitudinal state transitions, action-conditioned rollouts, causal identification, real-cohort validation, or prospective clinical utility.
legacy_cells.FX: Title/byline and abstract (PDF p. 2); Introduction and research gap (PDF pp. 2–4); Methods, including data setting, variables, model, estimation, and evaluation (PDF pp. 4–10); Results and Tables 1–2 plus figures and uncertainty results (PDF pp. 11–12); Discussion/limitations (PDF p. 13); Conclusion, funding, and data availability (PDF p. 14); references skimmed (PDF pp. 15–17). Full extracted PDF text read; table text was legible. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.

limitations: All17physical pages read including cover and36printed bibliography entries; all3figures and2tables visually inspected onp11–13; posterior/model equations p7–10 visually checked. No appendix.

DHS is discussed as intended data context, but results are simulated only. Actual DHS country/wave, sample size, selected predictors, DGP, training/test split, resampling and simulation replication details not given. R1 reported feasibility only; no R2/real-cohort claim.

VI/MCMC/dropout are listed as possible techniques without a reproducible choice, architecture dimensions, hyperparameters, diagnostics or data-generation code. Identifiability of latent truth and noise variance not established by replicated measurements or validation data.

Figure1 ROC shapes appear inconsistent with Table1 AUROCs; preserve table values as reported, no corrected AUC. Reliability plot lacks counts/bins; calibration-error definition and target of95% interval coverage unreported. No acceptance tolerance specified.

Joint posterior prints shared P(W) inside observation product; could overcount prior if literal. Do not silently repair or infer actual implementation. Figure?? unresolved crossreferencep11; Figure3 defines numerical noise levels but not scale units.

Hierarchical region/year random-effects extension is proposed, not demonstrated longitudinal dynamics. Measurement-error observation likelihood is static denoising, not clinician measurement-clock process.

ArticleCCBY license is not software/data license. Simulated data only on reasonable request; no code/weights release stated. Single-model source review, no independent human review or empirical replication.
